system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}

CONCEPT: Type-2 computability

ATOM FPPROG-C06-S2-03 (S2): A distribution $\mu$ on a computable metric space $(X,d,S)$ is computable if and only if it is samplable, meaning there is a computable, measure-preserving function from the fair-coin bit-stream space $(2^\omega,\mu_{iid})$ to $(X,\mu)$ that is computable on a domain of full measure.

EVIDENCE:
[FPPROG-p0098-s04] We call a distribution μ on X samplable if there is a computable function s : (2ω, μiid) ⇀(X, μ) such that s is computable on dom(s) of full-measure (i.e., μ(X) = 1) and is measure-preserving (i.e., μ = μiid ◦s−1).
[FPPROG-p0098-s05] Proposition 3.11 (Computable iff samplable, see Freer and Roy, 2010, Lem. 2 and Lem. 3).
[FPPROG-p0098-s06] A distribution μ ∈M(X) on computable metric space (X, d,S) is computable iff it is samplable.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- GROUNDED: hold — Delete “fair-coin”: the supplied sentences name μiid but do not specify its bit probabilities.
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Combines the computable–samplable equivalence with a separately assessable definition of samplability. / Combines the equivalence theorem (computable iff samplable) with the definition of a samplable distribution.
- L1_ONLY: hold — Keep the equivalence alone; the appended measure-preserving-map definition adds a second technical concept.
